messages:
tess: saw a big regression in eviction fairness on the 9am perf run. small tenants were being completely squeezed when a few prefixes went hot.

morgan: same. heatmap showed 3 prefixes using ~70% of resident blocks for a short burst.

tess: idea: 'prefix slimming' — at eviction time, trim low-entropy suffixes from the prefix keyspace so we treat many near-identical prefixes as one sizing unit instead of many tiny tenants. reduces fragmentation.

alex: interesting. that sounds like a normalization/compaction step for the cache key namespace. big question: correctness. if we collapse prefixes, do we risk returning stale/misattributed cached KV entries to clients?

tess: yeah that's the tradeoff. goal is to only slim when suffix variance is mostly ephemeral (high churn, low read locality). we'd tag entries with a prefix-shape id so lookups can still verify match.

sanjay: can you sketch the lookup path? i.e. where does runtime check the shape tag vs controller deciding to slim?

tess: rough flow: controller computes candidate shapes (histogram of suffix frequency per prefix). it pushes slim policy to runtime: e.g. {prefix: "user:conv:", shape_id: "s-12", mode: "merge-if-churn>0.7"}. runtime keeps both canonical keys and shape-tagged buckets. lookup does: 1) probe canonical exact key 2) if miss and shape exists, probe shape-bucket and verify metadata match.

li: verification cost sounds like extra probe + metadata compare. that adds latency on misses. we should only enable for cold-miss-heavy prefixes.

morgan: agree. also need a safe fallback to avoid false positives. maybe shape-bucket only used for eviction accounting, not for serving, initially.

tess: proposal: phase 1 = accounting-only: shape buckets influence eviction scores (fairshare weight), lookups unchanged. phase 2 = read-path probe enabled for shape-buckets after perf validation.

alex: phasing is good. other concern: multi-tenant isolation & billing — do we change how residency is attributed? billing must remain per-tenant. shape-based accounting would need attribution vectors.

sanjay: can do attribution by storing per-tenant residency counters inside the shape bucket (approx counters). but then we need bounded memory and lock contention model.

infra-bot: deploy-note: canary rollout target group = runtime-canary-evict-2. config flag: runtime.enable_prefix_slimming=false

li: ops question: how does this interact with pin/soft-pin APIs? if a tenant pins a prefix we must not slim it.

tess: yep. pin takes precedence and creates an anti-slim annotation. controller excludes pinned keyspaces from candidate shapes.

alex: long-term thought: maybe this is a signal that our prefix granularity is too fine. a refactor that introduces a small, stable namespace layer (prefix families) could solve many issues upstream instead of heuristic slimming. bigger project though.

morgan: can we add metrics to help decide? suggestion: eviction_share_by_prefix_family, shape_collision_rate, shape_probe_hit_latency. start with telemetry dashboard + nightly job that suggests candidates.

tess: agreed. i can open an RFC follow-up with: 1) accounting-only impl sketch + telemetry, 2) experiment plan and canary gating, 3) API boundary doc between controller and runtime (what fields we accept), 4) long-term "prefix family" refactor notes.

sanjay: SGTM. small ask: include a simple perf microbenchmark (single hotkey burst + mixed small tenants) so we can quantify fairness improvement and added miss latency.

li: also include a recovery plan: rollback flag and runbook if shape-probe causes correctness alerts.

tess: will do. tagging this for follow-up RFC. @morgan @alex can you review the draft tomorrow? :thumbsup:

morgan: yep

alex: on it

infra-bot: incident-note: none. no deploys in progress.
